migration_steps.activity: Inventory cryptographic assets: enumerate all device models, firmware versions, ECC P-256 usage (secure boot, TLS 1.2), cloud RSA-2048 endpoints, certificate chains, and key lifetimes. Document RAM/flash headroom per model.
prerequisites: Access to firmware source and build artifacts
Access to cloud TLS termination configuration
Device model list with memory specifications

migration_steps.activity: Benchmark candidate PQC algorithms (ML-KEM-512/768, ML-DSA-44/65) and hybrid constructions on representative device hardware. Measure RAM, flash, CPU cycles, and energy per operation against 64KB RAM / 256KB flash limits.
prerequisites: Reference PQC library builds (e.g., PQClean, mlkem-native, mldsa-native) available for target MCU
Hardware development boards for each device class

migration_steps.activity: Define hybrid cryptographic profile: ECC P-256 + ML-KEM for key establishment (TLS 1.3 hybrid key share) and ECC P-256 + ML-DSA for secure boot signatures. Specify algorithm roles, parameter sets, and fallback policy.
prerequisites: Review of IETF TLS hybrid key exchange drafts and NIST guidance
Cloud provider roadmap confirmation (AWS ML-KEM support forecast)

migration_steps.activity: Select and procure PQC-capable crypto library and toolchain for embedded targets. Verify licensing, FIPS/CAVP status, and long-term support commitments.

Implement hybrid PQC in firmware: integrate ML-KEM for TLS key establishment and ML-DSA for secure boot verification. Optimize for memory (e.g., streaming, on-the-fly key generation) and validate against 64KB RAM / 256KB flash.

Implement cloud-side hybrid PQC support: configure AWS load balancers/API gateways for hybrid TLS (ECC + ML-KEM) where available, and prepare ML-DSA certificate chain for backend authentication. Use AWS forecast support in 2027 as dependency.
prerequisites: AWS hybrid PQC feature availability (forecast 2027; interim use of hybrid TLS via third-party terminator if needed)

migration_steps.activity: Conduct interoperability and regression testing: device-to-cloud hybrid TLS handshake, secure boot with ML-DSA, performance under constrained memory, and backward compatibility with legacy ECC-only devices.
prerequisites: Test lab with device fleet and cloud staging environment

migration_steps.activity: Prepare production rollout plan and change management documentation. Schedule deployment windows outside change freeze (Nov 15–Jan 15).
Pilot deployment to a limited device cohort (e.g., 1% of fleet) with hybrid PQC firmware and cloud support. Monitor stability, performance, and security telemetry.
Full production rollout of hybrid PQC firmware via OTA updates, phased by device model. Maintain ECC fallback for legacy interoperability.
Establish continuous monitoring and cryptographic agility program: track NIST standards, vendor updates, and plan for pure PQC transition as device fleet refreshes over 10-year lifetime.

blockers.blocker: ML-KEM and ML-DSA memory footprint may exceed 64KB RAM / 256KB flash on some device models.
blockers.reason: NIST PQC algorithms require larger keys, ciphertexts, and working memory than ECC P-256; without optimization, devices may not fit both secure boot and TLS PQC.
blockers.resolution_required: Complete Step 2 benchmarks; if infeasible, adopt hybrid approach with ECC for secure boot and ML-KEM only for TLS, or hardware acceleration/secure element upgrade.

blockers.blocker: AWS ML-KEM support is forecast for 2027, not currently available.
blockers.reason: Cloud backend cannot terminate hybrid PQC TLS natively until AWS delivers support; relying on forecast risks schedule slip.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain written AWS roadmap commitment with dates; evaluate interim third-party TLS terminator or reverse proxy supporting hybrid PQC; plan cloud migration after AWS support confirmed.

blockers.blocker: Lack of finalized NIST standards for ML-KEM/ML-DSA in TLS and code signing profiles.
blockers.reason: Interoperability and certification depend on stable standards; premature implementation may require rework.
blockers.resolution_required: Monitor NIST and IETF drafts; implement against latest drafts with abstraction layer for easy update; participate in interoperability testing.

blockers.blocker: Change freeze from 2025-11-15 to 2026-01-15 prohibits production changes.
blockers.reason: Any production deployment or critical fix during freeze is disallowed, potentially delaying rollout.
blockers.resolution_required: Schedule all production changes outside freeze; use freeze period for documentation, training, and non-production testing only if permitted.

blockers.blocker: Budget of $150,000 may be insufficient for full hybrid PQC implementation across all device models and cloud backend.
blockers.reason: Costs include library licensing, hardware upgrades, testing, and cloud changes; scope may exceed budget.
blockers.resolution_required: Prioritize highest-risk models; use open-source libraries where possible; phase implementation; seek management approval for additional budget if needed.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Forecast: ML-KEM support in 2027 (not confirmed). No current hybrid PQC TLS termination on standard load balancers.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Written roadmap with committed dates; documentation of supported hybrid groups; SLA for PQC feature availability.

vendor_dependencies.vendor: Embedded crypto library provider (e.g., PQClean, wolfSSL, mbedTLS)
vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Varies: some open-source libraries have ML-KEM/ML-DSA implementations but may lack certification and optimization for constrained devices.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Memory footprint benchmarks on target MCU; FIPS/CAVP certification status; long-term support commitment; license terms.

vendor_dependencies.vendor: Certificate Authority (for ML-DSA code signing and TLS certificates)
vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Most CAs do not yet issue ML-DSA certificates; timelines uncertain.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Public announcement of ML-DSA certificate issuance; root program inclusion; pricing and SLA.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Current hardware may lack acceleration for PQC; secure elements may not support ML-DSA.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Hardware crypto acceleration specifications; secure element PQC support roadmap; migration path for existing devices.

algorithm_roles.ML-KEM: Post-quantum key establishment for TLS 1.3 hybrid key exchange (combined with ECC P-256) to protect cloud communication against quantum decryption. Not used for digital signatures.
algorithm_roles.ML-DSA: Post-quantum digital signatures for secure boot firmware verification and potentially for cloud backend authentication certificates. Not used for key establishment.
